story.title: A Row of Identical Men
story.text: Across the field stood a row of men, all dressed exactly alike.
story.narration: During the An Lushan rebellion in the Tang dynasty, Zhang Xun was holding a city. The enemy drew up their ranks outside, every coat of armour exactly the same, and there was no telling who was giving the orders — without finding that one man, you would not know where to push.

story.title: One Reed Arrow
story.text: One reed arrow flew over, and the man who turned to shout orders — that was him.
story.narration: Zhang Xun had arrows cut from reeds. A reed arrow cannot hurt anyone: it does not even sting. The man it hit did not care at all, but the people around him turned to look — and the one who turned and shouted orders was the leader, Yin Ziqi.

keyMoment.question: How do you find the leader among a row of men who all look exactly the same?

options.text: Shoot one harmless reed arrow and watch who reacts most
Drag them over one by one and ask
options.hint: Seize one and the rest scatter — you never get to the right man.
Guess wrong and the shot is wasted; you have to start over.

keyMoment.reveal: Find the one who matters most — take him, and the whole row falls apart.

misconceptions: With so many people, you can only catch them one by one
Taking the ringleader means knocking him down

quiz.question: What did Zhang Xun shoot across to test them?
quiz.explanation: The arrow was cut from reeds, so it could not hurt anyone — what he wanted was not to wound, but to see who reacted the most.

quiz.question: A crowd of classmates is making a noise on the playground. Who do you look at first?
options: Whoever makes everyone go quiet by speaking
quiz.explanation: The one everyone listens to is the leader of that crowd — finding him works far faster than shouting at each person in turn.

levelScript.hint: Try a reed dart on each
